<p class="tpl-lead" data-pagefind-weight="10">Information Security and Privacy Policy template: Ready-to-adopt consolidated security and privacy policy template for NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: every family policy in one document, with a variant per baseline (Low, Moderate, High, Privacy).</p>

## What it is

The Information Security and Privacy Policy is every family policy in one document, for an organization that would rather adopt one policy than twenty. It is assembled from the same sources as the [family policies](/templates/#policies), so its statements are theirs word for word. The sections every family policy shares are written once and meet each family's -1 control, such as [AC-1](/controls/ac/ac-1/). Each family then has its own part under Policy statements, with the accountable role of its family policy.

Each baseline variant includes only the controls in that baseline, taken from the NIST SP 800-53B profiles. The Program Management part is the same in every variant: SP 800-53B allocates no PM control to a baseline, and the organization carries them out once for all its systems. The Personally Identifiable Information Processing and Transparency family, which NIST places in the Privacy baseline only, is in the Privacy variant only. The Privacy variant has every family's Privacy-baseline statements: adopt it alongside the security variant wherever systems process personally identifiable information, or move its statements into the matching parts of the security variant so there is one document.

Adopt the ready-to-adopt edition: fill every highlighted field, delete any "Federal systems" section that does not apply, and have the accountable official approve it. The annotated edition adds guidance on why each section exists and what assessors look for. For any one scope, adopt either this policy or the family policies, not both. The [starter kit](/templates/starter-kit/) carries this policy at your baseline.

## Decisions to make first

The shared sections take one set of -1 values for every family: who receives the policy and the procedures, the managing official, and how often and after which events each is reviewed. Every other field is a family's own parameter. Record your values in the [decision worksheets](/templates/#decision-worksheets), one per family, and give each family's -1 rows the values you choose for the shared sections.

## Preview (Moderate baseline, annotated)

Each family's part is summarized here, with a link to its family policy; the downloads have the full text.

:::note[Guidance]
This policy brings every family policy into one document, as an alternative to adopting a policy per family. It is assembled from the same sources. The sections every family policy shares are written once, and each family's statements are in its own part under Policy statements. Each family's -1 control asks for a policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination and compliance, plus procedures, dissemination, a designated official and a review cycle; the shared sections meet those elements for every family listed under Control families. Assessors check each element for each family, so keep every shared section even when it is short. For any one scope, adopt either this policy or the family policies, not both, so each requirement has one source.
:::

### Purpose

This policy states what <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> requires for Information Security and Privacy, and who is accountable for meeting those requirements. (XX-1a.1(a))

### Scope

This policy applies at the <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: organization-level; mission/business process-level; system-level <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: organization-level</span></span> to every system that <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> owns or operates, or that is operated on its behalf, and to every person with access to those systems, including employees, contractors and partners. (XX-1a.1(a))

### Roles and responsibilities

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> is accountable for this policy and shall approve exceptions to it. (XX-1a.1(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the information security and privacy policy and procedures <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: Chief Information Security Officer</span></span> shall manage the development, documentation and dissemination of this policy and its procedures. (XX-1b)
- Each <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement this policy for their system and document how in the system security plan. (XX-1a.1(a))
- Each person within scope shall follow this policy and report suspected violations to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>. (XX-1a.1(a))

### Management commitment

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> approves this policy and shall provide the resources needed to implement it. (XX-1a.1(a))

### Coordination

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall coordinate this policy with the legal, privacy, human resources and procurement functions, and with the owners of related policies, before each approval. (XX-1a.1(a))

### Compliance

- This policy shall be consistent with the laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards and guidelines that apply to <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>, including <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: laws, regulations and standards that apply to the organization</span>. (XX-1a.1(b))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review compliance with this policy through the organization's assessment and continuous monitoring activities. (XX-1a.1(a))
- An exception to this policy shall be requested in writing, approved by the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>, time-limited and recorded with its compensating measures. (XX-1a.1(a))
- Violations of this policy shall be handled through the organization's sanctions process. (XX-1a.1(a))

### Approval and version history

<span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> records here the approval of each version of this document and each review of it, including a review that changes nothing. This is the record of the approval, review and update that SP 800-53 Rev. 5 asks for: item c of each family's -1 control for policies and procedures (for example AC-1c), PM-1a.4 and PM-1b for the information security program plan, and PL-2a.15, PL-2c and PL-2d for system plans.

:::note[Guidance]
Assessors ask for evidence that a document was approved, and that it was reviewed and updated on its cycle and after the events its review section names. This section is that evidence. It is the same in every template in the kit, so the records read alike across the program. Between them, the two tables hold what [NIST SP 800-18 Rev. 2](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/18/r2/final) (June 2026, section 3.2) says system plan approval, review records and change records include: the approvers' full names, roles, organizational titles, signatures and signature dates; who reviewed the plan, when, and the outcome; and for each change, its date, revision, who made it, the sections affected and what changed. Add a version history row for every review, including one that changes nothing: keep the version number, write "Reviewed, no change", and say what prompted the review, the scheduled cycle or an event. SP 800-18 Rev. 2 notes that document management systems can capture the signatures electronically; an approval recorded that way can stand in for the Signature column.
:::
